name: DataGrid
description: The data grid: sorting, filtering, grouping, pinned columns, row selection, detail rows, pagination and virtualization, with every part of it styled through the `datagrid` component tree rather than a stylesheet of its own.

props.name: component
props.description: Component name for style resolution. Default: 'datagrid'. Set to a custom name to use a different component style tree.

props.name: data
props.description: The rows. Virtualization means the length is not what is rendered — ten thousand is fine. Optional only because `def.dataSource` replaces it: with one set, this is not read at all.

props.name: def
props.description: Everything about the grid that is not the rows: the columns, the bars, the title, the row height.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show the loading sweep over the rows. The grid keeps whatever it is already showing underneath.

props.name: onSelectedRowKeysChange
props.description: Fires with every selected row key and why the selection changed.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: The older callback, whose event carries the keys *acted on* beside the selection. Both fire.

props.name: globalFilterValue
props.description: Controlled global filter value

props.name: onGlobalFilterChange
props.description: Fires with the global filter's new text, and whether it was typed or emptied.

props.name: columnFilters
props.description: Controlled column filters

props.name: onColumnFiltersChange
props.description: Fires with every column filter still set, and whether one was set or cleared.

props.name: filters
props.description: External predicate filters applied before global/column filters. Memoize with useMemo for performance.

props.name: expandedRowKeys
props.description: Controlled expanded detail row keys

props.name: onExpandedRowKeysChange
props.description: Fires with every expanded detail row key, and whether one was opened or shut.

props.name: expandedTreeKeys
props.description: Controlled open rows of a `def.treeData` tree. A separate list from `expandedRowKeys`, which is the detail panels: a row can have both, and they open different things.

props.name: onExpandedTreeKeysChange
props.description: Fires with every open tree row's key, and whether one was opened or shut.

props.name: page
props.description: Controlled current page (1-indexed). Used with pagination.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Controlled page size. Used with pagination and pageSizeOptions.

props.name: onPaginationChange
props.description: Fires with both pager values and why they changed — the page and the size move together, and a filter or a sort is what sends the grid back to the first page.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: The older page callback, whose second argument is the page size rather than the reason. Both fire.

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: The older page-size callback. Both fire.

props.name: onCellEditsChange
props.description: Fires with every edit the grid has accepted, oldest first — the stream an undo is built out of. It is the whole list rather than the one that changed, so a host keeps no history of its own, and it empties when `clearEdits()` says the host has saved them.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fires with the block of cells that is marked, or `undefined` once the grid has given it up. It reports the single current cell too, which is the degenerate range and what Ctrl+C acts on — so a status bar summing the selection is `range?.values()`, and a `reason` of `'select'` is the press or the arrow key that collapsed it back to one.

props.name: onSortingChange
props.description: Fires with the column and direction the grid is sorted by, or `undefined` once the sort is cleared.

props.name: onSortChange
props.type: (columnKey: Key | undefined, direction: SortDirection | undefined) => void
props.description: The older sort callback, whose two arguments are the column and the direction. Both fire.

props.name: onServerStateChange
props.description: Fires on any server-relevant state change with the full snapshot for an API call, and what moved.

keyboard.action: Enters the grid at one cell, not at every cell. Shift+Tab leaves it.
One cell along the row. At either end focus stays where it is.

Opens a shut row and shuts an open one; on a row that is already shut, Left steps out to its parent. Both follow the reading order, so they swap in a right-to-left grid, and on every other column they are the ordinary move along the row.
One row, keeping the column: through a group row or a detail panel with fewer cells, and through a grouped header whose cells cover several columns each.
The first or last cell of the row.
The first or last cell of the whole grid, scrolling there if it has not been rendered yet.
A screenful of rows at a time.
Sorts, on a sortable column header. On an editable cell, opens its editor. Anywhere else, steps into the cell's own control.
Steps into the cell's control even on a header, where Enter is spoken for by the sort; on an editable cell it opens the editor, as Enter does.
Opens the editor on that character, replacing the value the way a spreadsheet does.
Commits and hands the keyboard back to the cell. A value `def.onCellEdit` refuses keeps the editor open, with the message in a `role="alert"` and `aria-invalid` on the field.
Commits and opens the next or previous editable cell, along the row and on into the ones after it. With no next one it leaves the grid, as Tab does.
Hands the keyboard back from that control to the cell; from an editor it also throws the draft away.
Reaches the resizer of the header cell focus is on. Escape hands the keyboard back to the cell.
Moves the separator 16px, which widens or narrows the column exactly as dragging it would.
The narrowest the grid allows, or as wide as the grid itself.

a11y: `role="grid"` with `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount` over the whole data set and `aria-rowindex`/`aria-colindex` on what is rendered, so virtualization does not renumber the grid.

With `def.treeData` it is a `role="treegrid"` instead, and its rows carry `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize` and — valid only inside a treegrid — `aria-expanded`. The rows under a row are its siblings in the same rowgroup rather than its children, so those four are all a screen reader has to go on.
One cell is the tab stop, as APG's grid pattern specifies: the grid is entered once and the arrow keys move inside it, rather than every cell being a stop of its own.

A grid is not named by the rows in it — pass `def.title` and the grid points `aria-labelledby` at it. Everything the grid draws for itself is named after what it acts on ("Select row 4", "Filter Country"), and a selection change is announced through a `role="status"` region.
Each column resizer is a `role="separator"` — APG's window splitter — carrying the column's width on `aria-valuenow`, so the new width is read out as it changes.
